content.title: Justin Bieber’s Coachella soundcheck gives fans first taste of setlist - NOW Toronto
content.text: A viral soundcheck video hints at Justin Bieber’s setlist as he headlines the music festival this weekend, featuring hits from “Sorry” to “Peaches.” Justin Bieber is set to headline the 2026 Coachella music festival. (Courtesy: IG/lilbieber) What to know Justin Bieber headlines both weekends of Coachella 2026 (April 10–12, 17–19). Viral soundcheck videos hint at hits like “Sorry,” “Where Are Ü Now,” and older favourites like “Baby.” Bieber joins Canadian stars Drake and The Weeknd, alongside Beyoncé and Lady Gaga. Fans can catch the performance live via Coachella’s livestream, with potential setlist including “Peaches,” “Love Yourself,” and “Yummy.” Canada’s biggest pop star, Justin Bieber, is set to headline one of the biggest music festivals this weekend, Coachella, and a new viral video may have given fans an early glimpse of his setlist. Coachella takes place over two weekends, April 10-12 and 17-19, with Bieber headlining on Friday of both weekends. A recent viral clip captures Bieber’s soundcheck from the Coachella stage, reportedly audible from a nearby backyard. In the video, fans can hear hits like “Sorry” and “Where Are Ü Now.” Another user shared a video claiming to hear Bieber performing older tracks. The soundcheck reportedly included “Favorite Girl,” “Baby,” “One Less Lonely Girl,” and “All That Matters.” Bieber joins a prestigious lineup of headliners, including Beyoncé, Lady Gaga, and fellow Canadians Drake and The Weeknd, who have also graced the iconic festival stage. This headlining performance follows a prolific year for Bieber, who released two albums: Swag, nominated for Album of the Year at the 2026 Grammy Awards, and Swag II. Canadians hoping to watch Bieber take over the Coachella Valley from home can tune in via the Coachella LiveStream. In the meantime, fans can check out a playlist of songs that might appear on his setlist: “Daisies” “Yukon” “Love Yourself” “Peaches” “Boyfriend” “Never Say Never” “Yummy” “What Do You Mean”
